title: Plastic reeds and soaking cane reeds
summary: He rejects plastic reeds and explains how he wets reeds and sets them slightly below the tip.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

And I was told from someone that used the plastic reed, that after you get used to the plastic reed, you wouldn't be able to use the wooden reeds, the cane reeds, you know, after you get used to the plastic reed. So I decided not to fool with it, because I don't believe you could get a tone out of a plastic reed like you get out of a cane reed, for this reason, they don't get moisted.
It doesn't soak into them, I said.

No. You take a clarinet reed, you take a cane reed, most of the time you have to soak it in water by five minutes, to put it on your home, for it to blow right. But those things, they, those plastic reeds, you can't do anything with them.
Is that what you do with your reeds, Albert? You mean before you blow them, before you first get them? Yeah.

I wear it with my tongue, you see. Sometime you can take a reed out of the box and slap it on your horn, and it'll, and it'll suit you just right. Well, in that case you just use it.
